objects.description: End-user-visible URI class for parsing, inspecting, modifying, and printing HTTP-style URLs. Supports scheme/host/port/path/userinfo/fragment/query, with lazy parsing and a mutable query map. Thread-safety note: query() may rebuild the query string after SetQuery/RemoveQuery. Construction and destruction are trivial; internal resources are std::string, FlatMap, and status.
Lightweight splitter over a query string of the form key1=value1&key2&key3=value3. Provides iterative access to key, value pairs using the underlying butil::KeyValuePairsSplitter.

Helper to iterate a query string and selectively remove current key/value entries while producing a modified query. Wraps a QuerySplitter and tracks removals; call modified_query() after iteration/removals.

namespace brpc {

enum HttpMethod {
    HTTP_METHOD_DELETE      =   0,
    HTTP_METHOD_GET         =   1,
    HTTP_METHOD_HEAD        =   2,
    HTTP_METHOD_POST        =   3,
    HTTP_METHOD_PUT         =   4,
    HTTP_METHOD_CONNECT     =   5,
    HTTP_METHOD_OPTIONS     =   6,
    HTTP_METHOD_TRACE       =   7,
    HTTP_METHOD_COPY        =   8,
    HTTP_METHOD_LOCK        =   9,
    HTTP_METHOD_MKCOL       =   10,
    HTTP_METHOD_MOVE        =   11,
    HTTP_METHOD_PROPFIND    =   12,
    HTTP_METHOD_PROPPATCH   =   13,
    HTTP_METHOD_SEARCH      =   14,
    HTTP_METHOD_UNLOCK      =   15,
    HTTP_METHOD_REPORT      =   16,
    HTTP_METHOD_MKACTIVITY  =   17,
    HTTP_METHOD_CHECKOUT    =   18,
    HTTP_METHOD_MERGE       =   19,
    HTTP_METHOD_MSEARCH     =   20,  // M-SEARCH
    HTTP_METHOD_NOTIFY      =   21,
    HTTP_METHOD_SUBSCRIBE   =   22,

    HTTP_METHOD_PATCH       =   24,

    HTTP_METHOD_MKCALENDAR  =   26
};

// Returns literal description of `http_method'. "UNKNOWN" on not found.
const char *HttpMethod2Str(HttpMethod http_method);

// Convert case-insensitive `method_str' to enum HttpMethod.
// Returns true on success. 
bool Str2HttpMethod(const char* method_str, HttpMethod* method);

} // namespace brpc
objects.description: Enumeration of HTTP methods supported by brpc. Values map to standard HTTP/extension verbs (DELETE, GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, CONNECT, OPTIONS, TRACE, COPY, LOCK, MKCOL, MOVE, PROPFIND, PROPPATCH, SEARCH, UNLOCK, REPORT, MKACTIVITY, CHECKOUT, MERGE, M-SEARCH, NOTIFY, SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, PATCH, PURGE, MKCALENDAR). Use HttpMethod2Str to get a literal name and Str2HttpMethod to parse a case-insensitive method string into this enum.

objects.definition: const char *HttpReasonPhrase(int status_code);
objects.description: Pointer-returning API function that maps an HTTP status code to its RFC 2616 reason phrase. This is a function declaration, not a data type; included here only to note that no custom data types are defined in this header.
Collection of named integral constants representing HTTP/1.1 status codes per RFC 2616. These are plain integral constants, not enums or typedefs.

objects.definition: int ErrorCodeToStatusCode(int error_code);

Holds string-constant IDL names for the request and response types associated with an RPC method. Used to annotate RPCs with human-readable names for serialization/parsing in IDL services.

objects.definition:
// The identifier to be associated with a RPC call.
typedef bthread_id_t CallId;
objects.description: Opaque identifier (typedef of bthread_id_t) representing an RPC call instance, used with helper functions like StartCancel and Join.
Enum configuring how a ProgressiveAttachment writer stops: FORCE_STOP fails the underlying socket immediately when idle or server stops; WAIT_FOR_STOP waits for graceful stop.

objects.definition: typedef butil::FlatMap<std::string, std::string> UserFieldsMap;
objects.description: Map of arbitrary key/value string pairs carried alongside requests/responses in the baidu_std protocol. Exposed via Controller::request_user_fields() and response_user_fields().

Primary per-RPC controller implementing google::protobuf::RpcController for brpc. It encapsulates client/server-side settings, attachments, HTTP headers, timeouts, retries, compression/checksum options, progressive read/write, authentication context, IDs, and error reporting. Non-copyable; reusable via Reset(). Inner types (Inheritable, LogPrefixDummy, CompletionInfo, ClientSettings, Call) are defined inside the class and used to carry inheritable context, logging prefix mechanism, completion handling, client setting snapshots, and per-attempt call state. Construction is via stack or new; lifecycles are managed by user code and brpc runtime during RPCs.
Lightweight context that can be passed from a server-side Controller to child Controllers to inherit session-level identifiers (log_id and request_id).
Helper used by logging macros to print contextual prefixes derived from a Controller. Returned by Controller::LogPrefix().

Configuration bundle for brpc::Channel connections, timeouts, retries, backup requests, SSL, auth, naming, load balancing, and health checks. Some members point to external policy objects not owned by the options. Constructor initializes sensible defaults; mutable_ssl_options allocates SSL options on demand.

Client-side RPC channel encapsulating connection(s) to one or more servers, load balancing, and request invocation. Constructed with default constructor; must be initialized via one of the Init overloads before use. Provides synchronous/asynchronous CallMethod and utility APIs. Not copyable.
Enumeration indicating whether a wrapper or owner object is responsible for deleting a brpc::Channel instance.

Config structure for brpc::Server. Holds server-wide settings such as timeouts, protocol enablement, SSL, thread/bthread initialization, auth/interceptor hooks, per-session/thread data factories, builtin service exposure, HTTP2, Redis/RTMP adaptors, and master/proxy services. Some pointers are owned by Server as documented in comments. Constructed with defaults via ServerOptions().
Lightweight snapshot of basic server stats: active connection count and numbers of user and builtin services. Filled by Server::GetStat().
Enum describing ownership semantics when services are registered to a Server: either owned and deleted by the server, or managed by the user.

Options controlling how a google::protobuf::Service is added to a Server: ownership, RESTful path mappings and related flags, HTTP body to protobuf conversion, JSON compatibility flags, and progressive read enablement.
Simple range type representing [min_port, max_port] used when starting a Server on any available port in the range.

Main RPC server class. Manages service registration, startup/shutdown, request dispatch, SSL certificate management, concurrency limits, and various builtin and monitoring features. Contains nested types for service/method metadata, status, and TLS options. Constructed via Server(); lifecycle controlled by Start/Stop/Join. Many forward-declared collaborators are referenced but defined elsewhere.

Represents a Redis request that can pipeline multiple commands. Provides APIs to add commands in various forms and to serialize the request buffer. Inherits NonreflectableMessage for protobuf-like behaviors.
Represents a Redis response that may include multiple replies due to pipelining. Provides parsing from IOBuf and accessors for individual replies. Inherits NonreflectableMessage.
Container and registry for RedisCommandHandler instances keyed by command name. Assign an instance to ServerOption.redis_service to enable Redis support on the server.

Enumeration of outcomes for a RedisCommandHandler::Run invocation: handled, continue (e.g., transactions), or batched (defer and batch results). Note: this is an enum type; use by value, not as a pointer.

Per-connection context for the Redis protocol on a server socket. Tracks service, transaction handler, batching state, parser, arena, and an optional authenticated session object. Inherits Destroyable for lifecycle integration.

Abstract handler interface for processing Redis commands. Implement Run to handle a command; override transactional behavior via NewTransactionHandler and the context-aware Run overload. Default Run returns REDIS_CMD_HANDLED.

objects.definition: class RedisCommandParser;
objects.description: Forward declaration only. Parser for Redis commands used inside RedisConnContext. No definition provided in this header.

A non-reflectable brpc message that builds a pipelined Memcached binary protocol request. Supports queuing multiple operations (get, set/add/replace/append/prepend, delete, flush, incr/decr, touch, version) into an internal IOBuf and sending them in one RPC. Tracks pipelined operation count and exposes protobuf-like interfaces required by brpc. Construction/destruction details are not visible here; actual encoding occurs via private helpers.

A non-reflectable brpc message that parses and iterates through a pipelined Memcached binary protocol response. Provides pop-style methods matching the queued request order to extract results for get/set/add/replace/append/prepend/delete/flush/incr/decr/touch/version. Includes Status enum for memcached response codes and maintains an internal buffer with last-error string. Protobuf-like interfaces are provided for brpc integration.

url must be a syntactically valid HTTP/URL; on failure, the function returns -1 and status() describes the error.

functions.name: brpc::URI::operator=

requirements: url may include leading/trailing spaces which are ignored.

functions.description: Returns the status of the most recent SetHttpURL or operator= call, indicating success or parse error details.

functions.name: brpc::URI::schema

functions.name: brpc::URI::host
functions.description: Returns the host component of the URI. Empty if unset.

functions.name: brpc::URI::path
functions.description: Returns the path component of the URI. Empty if unset.

functions.name: brpc::URI::fragment
functions.description: Returns the fragment component (portion after '#'). Empty if unset.

requirements: If queries are mutated (SetQuery/RemoveQuery), external synchronization is required when calling query() concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: brpc::URI::GenerateH2Path

requirements: h2_path must be a non-null pointer to a std::string.

functions.name: brpc::URI::set_scheme
functions.description: Overwrites the scheme component. The input must be a valid scheme string.

Caller is responsible for ensuring validity; no validation is guaranteed.

functions.name: brpc::URI::set_schema
functions.description: Deprecated alias of set_scheme(). Overwrites the scheme component.
requirements: The input MUST be valid per URI scheme rules.
Caller is responsible for ensuring validity; no validation is guaranteed.

functions.name: brpc::URI::set_path
functions.description: Overwrites the path component. The input must be a valid path string.
requirements: The input MUST be a valid path per URI syntax.
Caller is responsible for ensuring validity; no validation is guaranteed.

functions.name: brpc::URI::set_host
functions.description: Overwrites the host component. The input must be a valid host.
requirements: The input MUST be a valid host.
Caller is responsible for ensuring validity; no validation is guaranteed.

functions.name: brpc::URI::set_port
functions.description: Overwrites the port component.
requirements: port must be a valid port number or -1 to indicate unset; the header does not enforce range, but typical valid range is 0–65535 (inferred; exact enforcement unknown).

functions.name: brpc::URI::SetHostAndPort
functions.description: Parses and sets the host and optionally the port from a combined string like "example.com:80".
requirements: host_and_optional_port must be syntactically valid in the form "host[:port]".
Caller is responsible for ensuring validity; no validation is guaranteed by the setter note.

functions.name: brpc::URI::SetH2Path
functions.description: Sets path, query, and fragment from a combined string in the form "path?query#fragment".
requirements: h2_path must be a non-null C-string in the form "path?query#fragment".
The input MUST be valid per the note on setters; caller must ensure correctness.

functions.name: brpc::URI::GetQuery
functions.signature: const std::string* brpc::URI::GetQuery(const char* key) const
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the value of the given CASE-SENSITIVE query key, or NULL if the key does not exist.
requirements: key comparison is case-sensitive.
The returned pointer is invalidated after SetQuery() or SetHttpURL().

functions.name: brpc::URI::SetQuery
functions.signature: void brpc::URI::SetQuery(const std::string& key, const std::string& value)
functions.description: Adds or overwrites a query key/value pair in the URI. Marks the query as modified so that query() will regenerate the raw string when needed.
requirements: key and value are used verbatim; no URL-encoding is performed by the declaration (encoding expectations are unknown).
Invalidates existing query iterators and value pointers.

functions.name: brpc::URI::RemoveQuery
functions.description: Removes the query parameter with the given CASE-SENSITIVE key. Returns 1 if removed, 0 if not found. Marks the query as modified.
requirements: key comparison is case-sensitive.
Invalidates existing query iterators and value pointers after mutation.

functions.name: brpc::URI::QueryBegin
functions.description: Returns a const iterator to the beginning of the parsed query map.
requirements: Iterators are invalidated after calling SetQuery() or SetHttpURL().

functions.name: brpc::URI::QueryEnd
functions.description: Returns a const iterator to the end of the parsed query map.
requirements: Iterators are invalidated after calling SetQuery() or SetHttpURL().

functions.name: brpc::URI::QueryCount
functions.description: Returns the number of key/value pairs in the parsed query map.

functions.name: brpc::URI::PrintWithoutHost
functions.description: Writes the URI components from path onward (path, query, fragment) to the provided output stream.
requirements: os must be a valid std::ostream reference.

functions.name: brpc::URI::Print

requirements: os must be a valid std::ostream reference.

requirements: url must point to a valid, null-terminated URL string.

requirements: os must be a valid std::ostream reference.
uri must reference a valid brpc::URI.

functions.name: brpc::QuerySplitter::QuerySplitter

functions.description: Constructs a splitter over the half-open range [str_begin, str_end) parsing key/value pairs separated by '&' and '='.
requirements: str_begin and str_end must define a valid character range with str_begin <= str_end.

functions.name: brpc::QueryRemover::QueryRemover
functions.description: Initializes a helper to iterate a query string and selectively remove keys. After iteration/removals, call modified_query() to obtain the resulting query.
requirements: str must be a non-null pointer to the original query string and must outlive the QueryRemover instance and its iteration.

functions.name: brpc::QueryRemover::key
functions.description: Returns the key of the current query element as a StringPiece.
requirements: Must be called when the internal splitter is in a valid state (i.e., during iteration).

functions.name: brpc::QueryRemover::value
functions.description: Returns the value of the current query element as a StringPiece.
requirements: Must be called when the internal splitter is in a valid state (i.e., during iteration).

functions.name: brpc::QueryRemover::key_and_value
functions.description: Returns the raw "key[=value]" slice of the current query element.
requirements: Must be called when the internal splitter is in a valid state (i.e., during iteration).

functions.name: brpc::QueryRemover::operator++
functions.description: Advances the remover/splitter to the next query element (prefix increment).
requirements: Must be used while iteration is valid; advancing past the end yields falsy state via operator const void*().

functions.name: brpc::QueryRemover::operator++
functions.description: Advances the remover/splitter to the next query element (postfix increment).
requirements: Must be used while iteration is valid; advancing past the end yields falsy state via operator const void*().

functions.name: brpc::QueryRemover::operator const void*
functions.description: Contextual boolean conversion indicating whether the internal splitter is in a valid (non-end) state.

functions.name: brpc::QueryRemover::remove_current_key_and_value
functions.description: Marks the current key/value to be removed from the resulting modified_query(). Calling multiple times on the same element has no additional effect.
requirements: Must be called while positioned at a valid element during iteration.

functions.name: brpc::QueryRemover::modified_query
functions.description: Returns the modified query string after any removals. Subsequent calls return the same result unless further removals occur during iteration.

functions.signature: void brpc::append_query(std::string* query_string, const butil::StringPiece& key, const butil::StringPiece& value)
functions.description: Appends key=value to query_string, inserting '?' or '&' as needed depending on the current contents. Handles empty strings and path-with-optional-question-mark cases.
requirements: query_string must be a non-null pointer to a std::string.
key and value are appended verbatim; encoding behavior is unspecified in the header.

functions.name: brpc::HttpMethod2Str
functions.description: Maps a brpc::HttpMethod enum value to its canonical method name string (e.g., HTTP_METHOD_GET -> "GET"). If the value is not recognized, returns the literal string "UNKNOWN". Typical usage is for logging, diagnostics, or formatting HTTP requests.
requirements: http_method should be a valid brpc::HttpMethod enumerator to avoid receiving "UNKNOWN".
The returned pointer refers to a constant, static string literal; the caller must not modify or free it.

functions.name: brpc::Str2HttpMethod
functions.signature: bool brpc::Str2HttpMethod(const char* method_str, brpc::HttpMethod* method)
functions.description: Parses a case-insensitive HTTP method name (e.g., "GET", "post") and writes the corresponding brpc::HttpMethod enum to the output parameter. Returns true on successful conversion; otherwise returns false and no specific output is guaranteed. Useful for parsing incoming HTTP requests or user input into the enum form.
requirements: method_str must be a non-null, null-terminated C-string containing an HTTP method name.
method must be a non-null pointer to writable storage for a brpc::HttpMethod result.
Comparison is case-insensitive; callers may pass mixed-case method strings.
Callers must check the boolean return value to determine if parsing succeeded before using *method.

functions.name: brpc::HttpReasonPhrase
functions.description: Returns the HTTP reason phrase string for the given numeric status code. If the code is unknown, returns a string of the form "Unknown status code (|status_code|)". The function is thread-safe and never returns NULL. Note: the returned pointer may refer to memory that is reused on subsequent calls; do not cache the pointer—copy the string if you need to retain it.
requirements: Input status_code may be any integer; unknown values yield an "Unknown status code" message.
The returned pointer is valid only until a subsequent call to this function potentially reuses the underlying memory; copy the string if persistence is needed.
Do not cache the returned pointer in containers or long-lived storage.
No NULL will be returned according to the documentation; callers should still be robust to unexpected inputs by handling the "Unknown status code" string.

functions.name: brpc::ErrorCodeToStatusCode

requirements: No explicit restrictions on error_code are documented in this header.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate valid HTTP/WS URLs emphasizing:
# - scheme in {http, https, ws, wss}
# - hostname: [a-z0-9.-], non-empty, <=255, labels 1-63, no leading/trailing hyphen
# - optional port 1..65535
# - path starting with '/', limited charset
# - optional simple query
# The fuzzing stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times (host, path) and FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) for toggles/ports.
# Our buffer will contain multiple newline-separated fields so the harness can consume
# sequential strings/ints deterministically. Common fuzzers often map FUZZ_PARAM_STR to
# sequential slices; here we provide a compact, self-descriptive format:
#   scheme\n
#   host\n
#   path\n
#   port_flag (0/1)\n
#   port (1..65535)\n
#   query_flag (0/1)\n
# Additional lines are safe; consumers that only take some parameters will still see
# valid strings when they read from the beginning.

SCHEMES = ["http", "https", "ws", "wss"]

def _rand_hostname(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build 1-5 labels, each 1-20 chars, RFC-like constraints.
    nlabels = rng.randint(1, 5)
    labels: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(nlabels):
        length = rng.randint(1, 20)
        # First/last must be alnum, interior may include '-'
        if length == 1:
            label = rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)
        else:
            first = rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)
            middle_len = max(0, length - 2)
            middle_chars = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-"
            middle = ''.join(rng.choice(middle_chars) for _ in range(middle_len))
            last = rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)
            label = first + middle + last
        labels.append(label)
    host = '.'.join(labels)
    # Truncate to 255 if necessary by dropping leading labels
    while len(host) > 255 and len(labels) > 1:
        labels = labels[1:]
        host = '.'.join(labels)
    return host or "localhost"

def _rand_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Path with 0-8 segments, each 0-12 chars from allowed set
    segs = []
    nseg = rng.randint(0, 8)
    allowed = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_- ."
    for _ in range(nseg):
        seglen = rng.randint(0, 12)
        seg = ''.join(rng.choice(allowed) for _ in range(seglen))
        # Replace spaces with '.' to remain conservative
        seg = seg.replace(' ', '.')
        segs.append(seg)
    path = "/" + "/".join(segs)
    if len(path) > 2048:
        path = path[:2048]
    # Ensure no trailing slash duplication
    path = path.replace("//", "/")
    if not path.startswith("/"):
        path = "/" + path
    return path

def _rand_port(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    return rng.randint(1, 65535)

def _rand_flag(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    return rng.randint(0, 1)

def _build_one_url(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    scheme = rng.choice(SCHEMES)
    host = _rand_hostname(rng)
    path = _rand_path(rng)
    with_port = _rand_flag(rng)
    port = _rand_port(rng)
    with_query = _rand_flag(rng)
    # Compose URL string for convenience as well
    url = f"{scheme}://{host}"
    if with_port:
        url += f":{port}"
    url += path
    if with_query:
        url += "?k=v"
    # Return a multi-line package of fields plus full URL first for flexibility
    parts = [url, scheme, host, path, str(with_port), str(port), str(with_query)]
    return "\n".join(parts)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Generate several candidate URLs/fields so multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls can draw distinct values.
    count = rng.randint(1, 6)
    chunks = []
    for _ in range(count):
        chunks.append(_build_one_url(rng))
    payload = "\n\n".join(chunks)
    data = payload.encode("utf-8")
    # Ensure size limit
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We generate bytes that the fuzzer will expose via FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# The stubs construct URLs and H2 paths from these strings, sanitizing to safe chars.
# Our goal: provide initial interesting buffers containing multiple candidate strings
# separated in a simple, parseable way for the harness. Common pattern is that fuzzers
# read consecutively from a single input buffer to fulfill FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
# We therefore pack several variable-length ASCII segments with diverse characters
# that, after the stub's sanitization, yield meaningful variations (hosts, paths).
#
# Strategy:
# - Emit a sequence of N segments, each length-prefixed with 1 byte (0..255), followed by bytes.
# - Compose segments to cover:
#   * host-like strings (letters, digits, dots, dashes), including IPv4 and IPv6-ish (will be sanitized)
#   * path-like strings with '/', '_', '-', '.' and case variety
#   * segments including characters that will be stripped by the stub to test empty-to-default behavior
#   * long path segment near cap (will be truncated to 2048 by stub)
# - Limit total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# The harness isn't specified, but this length-prefixed format is commonly supported in libFuzzer-style
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR providers; at minimum, each call will get the next slice. If not, providing a flat buffer
# with many useful tokens still gives good initial coverage.

SAFE_HOST_CHARS = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + ".-"
SAFE_PATH_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "/_- ."  # include space and dot; spaces get removed by stub filter


def _rand_host(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix of domain labels, possibly with digits and dashes
    labels = []
    nlabels = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for i in range(nlabels):
        l = rng.randint(1, 10)
        s = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + '-') for _ in range(l)).strip('-')
        if not s:
            s = 'a'
        labels.append(s)
    host = '.'.join(labels)
    # Occasionally return IPv4-like
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        host = '.'.join(str(rng.randint(0, 255)) for _ in range(4))
    return host


def _rand_noisy_host(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Include many unsupported chars which will be stripped by stub, possibly becoming empty
    noisy = ''.join(rng.choice(string.printable) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 16)))
    core = _rand_host(rng)
    tail = ''.join(rng.choice("[]{}!@#$%^&*()+=,;:\\|/?<>\"'\t\n") for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 8)))
    return noisy + core + tail


def _rand_path(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    # Ensure leading '/'
    segs: List[str] = []
    remaining = target_len
    while remaining > 0:
        part_len = rng.randint(1, min(remaining, 16))
        part = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '_-.') for _ in range(part_len))
        segs.append(part)
        remaining -= part_len
    path = '/' + '/'.join(segs)
    # Occasionally add consecutive slashes and dots
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        path = path.replace('/', '//' if rng.random() < 0.5 else '/./')
    return path


def _rand_queryish(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Although stubs hardcode query, provide segments that could be used elsewhere
    keys = ['k', 'a', 'c', 'user', 'id', 'q']
    vals = ['v', 'b', 'd', 'alice', '123', 'xyz']
    n = rng.randint(1, 4)
    pairs = []
    for _ in range(n):
        k = rng.choice(keys)
        v = rng.choice(vals)
        pairs.append(f"{k}={v}")
    return '&'.join(pairs)


def _make_segment(s: str) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    # length prefix in 1 byte; truncate if necessary
    if len(b) > 255:
        b = b[:255]
    return bytes([len(b)]) + b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    segments: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Good host
    segments.append(_make_segment(_rand_host(rng)))
    # 2) Noisy host that may sanitize to empty (stub defaults to localhost/example.com)
    segments.append(_make_segment(_rand_noisy_host(rng)))
    # 3) Short simple path
    segments.append(_make_segment(_rand_path(rng, rng.randint(1, 20))))
    # 4) Long path near 2048 limit
    long_len = rng.randint(256, 600)
    segments.append(_make_segment(_rand_path(rng, long_len)))
    # 5) Another host variant
    segments.append(_make_segment(_rand_host(rng)))
    # 6) Another path variant with underscores and dots
    base = '/'.join(['', 'api', 'v1', 'users_' + str(rng.randint(0, 999)), 'profile.' + rng.choice(['json','html','xml'])])
    segments.append(_make_segment(base))
    # 7) A segment of characters that will largely be stripped by the stub
    junk = ''.join(rng.choice(" \t\n\r\x00\x01\x02[]{}!@#$%^&*()+=,;:\\|/?<>\"'") for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 40)))
    segments.append(_make_segment(junk))
    # 8) Query-like segment (may be unused but safe)
    segments.append(_make_segment(_rand_queryish(rng)))
    # 9) Mixed-case path to test case handling
    mix = '/' + ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '_-./') for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 40)))
    segments.append(_make_segment(mix))

    data = b''.join(segments)
    # Ensure max size <= 4096
    return data[:4096]

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Target formats observed in stubs:
# - Full HTTP/WS URL: scheme://host[:port]/path[?query]
# - H2 path: /path[?query][#fragment]
# - Query strings used by QuerySplitter: key=value&k2=v2&k3
# This generator returns a bytes buffer intended to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME
# with valid and interesting values. We encode multiple candidate strings
# concatenated with NUL separators so the fuzzer can pick different slices.

SCHEMES = [b"http", b"https", b"ws", b"wss"]

HOST_LABEL_CHARS = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-"
PATH_SEG_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_./"
QUERY_KEY_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.*"
QUERY_VAL_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.~/:%"

MAX_TOTAL_SIZE = 4096


def _rand_choice(rnd: random.Random, s: str, lo: int, hi: int) -> str:
    n = rnd.randint(lo, hi)
    return "".join(rnd.choice(s) for _ in range(n))


def _gen_host(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate mixture: domain, localhost, numeric IPv4-like
    mode = rnd.randint(0, 3)
    if mode == 0:
        labels = []
        nlab = rnd.randint(2, 4)
        for _ in range(nlab):
            # label length 1..10, avoid leading/trailing '-'
            core = _rand_choice(rnd, HOST_LABEL_CHARS, 1, 10)
            core = core.strip('-') or 'a'
            labels.append(core)
        return ".".join(labels)
    elif mode == 1:
        return "localhost"
    elif mode == 2:
        # IPv4 dotted-decimal
        return ".".join(str(rnd.randint(1, 254)) for _ in range(4))
    else:
        # include subdomains and hyphens
        base = _gen_host(rnd)
        sub = _rand_choice(rnd, HOST_LABEL_CHARS, 3, 8).strip('-') or 'sub'
        return f"{sub}.{base}"


def _gen_path(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Ensure leading '/'. Include multiple segments; optionally long.
    segs = []
    nseg = rnd.randint(1, 6)
    for _ in range(nseg):
        seg = _rand_choice(rnd, PATH_SEG_CHARS.replace('/', ''), 0, 12)
        segs.append(seg)
    path = "/" + "/".join(segs)
    # Optionally ensure a file-like ending
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        ext = rnd.choice([".html", ".txt", ".json", ".bin", ""])
        if not path.endswith('/'):
            path += ext
    return path


def _gen_query_pairs(rnd: random.Random) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
    # Mix of k=v and lone keys; include duplicates and case variations
    pairs = []
    n = rnd.randint(1, 8)
    for i in range(n):
        k = _rand_choice(rnd, QUERY_KEY_CHARS, 1, rnd.randint(4, 16))
        # sometimes duplicate a key
        if rnd.random() < 0.2 and pairs:
            k = rnd.choice(pairs)[0]
        if rnd.random() < 0.25:
            # lone key
            pairs.append((k, None))
        else:
            v = _rand_choice(rnd, QUERY_VAL_CHARS, 0, rnd.randint(4, 24))
            # occasionally include percent-escapes which should be kept as-is
            if rnd.random() < 0.2:
                v = v + "%" + rnd.choice("0123456789ABCDEF") + rnd.choice("0123456789ABCDEF")
            pairs.append((k, v))
    return pairs


def _pairs_to_query(pairs: List[Tuple[str, str]]) -> str:
    parts = []
    for k, v in pairs:
        if v is None:
            parts.append(k)
        else:
            parts.append(f"{k}={v}")
    return "&".join(parts)


def _gen_h2_path(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    path = _gen_path(rnd)
    s = path
    if rnd.random() < 0.9:
        s += "?" + _pairs_to_query(_gen_query_pairs(rnd))
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        frag = _rand_choice(rnd, string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.", 1, 12)
        s += "#" + frag
    return s


def _gen_full_url(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    scheme = rnd.choice(SCHEMES).decode()
    host = _gen_host(rnd)
    url = f"{scheme}://{host}"
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        url += f":{rnd.randint(1, 65535)}"
    url += _gen_path(rnd)
    if rnd.random() < 0.85:
        url += "?" + _pairs_to_query(_gen_query_pairs(rnd))
    return url


def _gen_query_only(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    return _pairs_to_query(_gen_query_pairs(rnd))


def _make_backing_slices(rnd: random.Random, base: str) -> List[str]:
    # For QuerySplitter(begin,end), provide a backing buffer and several
    # in-range slices (begin<=end) that look like sub-queries.
    slices = []
    if not base:
        return slices
    n = len(base)
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(2, 6)):
        i = rnd.randint(0, n)
        j = rnd.randint(0, n)
        if i > j:
            i, j = j, i
        slices.append(base[i:j])
    return slices


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    pieces: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Several well-formed full URLs for SetHttpURL/operator=
    for _ in range(4):
        pieces.append(_gen_full_url(rnd).encode('utf-8'))

    # 2) Several valid h2-path strings for SetH2Path
    for _ in range(3):
        pieces.append(_gen_h2_path(rnd).encode('utf-8'))

    # 3) Rich query strings for QuerySplitter/QueryRemover
    for _ in range(4):
        q = _gen_query_only(rnd)
        pieces.append(q.encode('utf-8'))
        # Provide sub-slices from the same backing content to exercise [begin,end)
        for sl in _make_backing_slices(rnd, q):
            if sl:
                pieces.append(sl.encode('utf-8'))

    # 4) Edge-case but valid minimal inputs
    pieces.append(b"/")  # minimal path
    pieces.append(b"k=v")  # minimal query
    pieces.append(b"key-only")  # lone key in query
    pieces.append(b"http://localhost/")  # simplest absolute URL

    # 5) Long but valid path and query within size budget
    long_path = "/" + "a" * rnd.randint(100, 600)
    long_query = _pairs_to_query([("k", "v" * rnd.randint(50, 150))])
    pieces.append((long_path + "?" + long_query).encode('utf-8'))

    # Join with NUL separators so consumer can split or pick arbitrary slices
    buf = b"\x00".join(pieces)
    if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL_SIZE:
        buf = buf[:MAX_TOTAL_SIZE]
    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs for FUZZ_PARAM_STR used to build an HTTP/2 path
# string for brpc::URI::SetH2Path. The stub filters input to characters in
# [A-Za-z0-9/_-.] and prefixes with '/'. It may optionally append a fixed
# query (?k=v) and fragment (#frag) based on other FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int).
# We therefore generate a path component consisting of segments and optional
# allowed characters, ensuring variety in depth and length while staying <= 2048
# characters so the stub does not truncate most of our interesting cases.
#
# The fuzzer framework will read this buffer and use it as FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# We produce bytes of a UTF-8 string comprised only of accepted characters so
# all of them survive the stub’s filter.

_ALLOWED = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "/_.-"

def _rand_segment(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(_ALLOWED) for _ in range(n))

def _build_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a strategy to exercise different path shapes
    strategy = rng.randint(0, 6)
    segments: List[str] = []

    if strategy == 0:
        # Deep hierarchy with short names
        depth = rng.randint(2, 20)
        segments = [_rand_segment(rng, 1, 4) for _ in range(depth)]
    elif strategy == 1:
        # Few long segments
        count = rng.randint(1, 5)
        segments = [_rand_segment(rng, 10, 60) for _ in range(count)]
    elif strategy == 2:
        # Mix of empty and dot/underscore heavy segments (still valid after filter)
        count = rng.randint(3, 15)
        for _ in range(count):
            kind = rng.randint(0, 2)
            if kind == 0:
                segments.append(_rand_segment(rng, 1, 8))
            elif kind == 1:
                segments.append('.' * rng.randint(1, 4))
            else:
                segments.append('_' * rng.randint(1, 6))
    elif strategy == 3:
        # Numeric-heavy segments
        count = rng.randint(2, 12)
        segments = [''.join(rng.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 12))) for _ in range(count)]
    elif strategy == 4:
        # Alternating short and long
        count = rng.randint(2, 14)
        for i in range(count):
            segments.append(_rand_segment(rng, 1, 3) if (i % 2 == 0) else _rand_segment(rng, 15, 40))
    elif strategy == 5:
        # Many single-char segments
        count = rng.randint(5, 60)
        segments = [rng.choice(_ALLOWED) for _ in range(count)]
    else:
        # Heaviest allowed length near the stub cap
        # Build a repeated pattern to get close to 1800 chars after join
        unit = _rand_segment(rng, 3, 10)
        repeat = max(1, 1800 // (len(unit) + 1))
        segments = [unit] * repeat

    # Compose the path. The stub will prefix with '/', but we can provide a
    # path string used to extend after that prefix via filtering loop. Using
    # leading/trailing slashes in raw string increases chances of // and trailing '/'.
    path_body = '/'.join(segments)

    # Randomly add leading/trailing slashes in the FUZZ_PARAM_STR; they survive filter
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        path_body = '/' + path_body
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        path_body = path_body + '/'

    # Ensure final length under 2048 so most content is kept pre-truncation in stub
    if len(path_body) > 2048:
        path_body = path_body[:2048]

    return path_body

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build multiple variants and pick one to increase diversity under same seed space
    variants = []
    for _ in range(3):
        variants.append(_build_path(rng))
    chosen = rng.choice(variants)

    # Return UTF-8 bytes; characters are ASCII-safe.
    return chosen.encode('utf-8')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs used by brpc URI query utilities and MemcacheRequest ops in the stubs.
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR is consumed as keys/values for query strings and memcache keys. The stubs often
# sanitize to [A-Za-z0-9_.-] and cap lengths, so we primarily generate such tokens with variety in
# length and character distribution. We also sometimes include path-like prefixes for append_query cases.
# The fuzzer harness will split this buffer and provide different slices to FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_.-"

def _rand_token(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, allow_empty: bool = False) -> str:
    if allow_empty and r.random() < 0.1:
        return ""
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Bias: start with letter to form valid identifiers sometimes
    if n > 0 and r.random() < 0.6:
        first = r.choice(string.ascii_letters)
        rest_len = n - 1
        rest = "".join(r.choices(SAFE_CHARS, k=rest_len)) if rest_len > 0 else ""
        return first + rest
    return "".join(r.choices(SAFE_CHARS, k=n))

def _rand_path_prefix(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate "/", "/path", "/p?q=r" etc. Useful for append_query initial states.
    choice = r.random()
    if choice < 0.25:
        return ""
    if choice < 0.5:
        return "/"
    if choice < 0.75:
        return "/" + _rand_token(r, 1, 8)
    # include existing query
    return "/" + _rand_token(r, 1, 6) + "?" + _rand_token(r, 1, 6) + "=" + _rand_token(r, 1, 6)

def _build_corpus(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    corpus: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Common short keys/values likely to collide across runs
    common = [b"k", b"v", b"a", b"b", b"x", b"y", b"m", b"n", b"id", b"q", b"page", b"token", b"session"]
    corpus.extend(common)

    # 2) Random safe tokens at lengths that match stub caps (<=64, <=128, <=256)
    for L in (1, 2, 5, 16, 32, 48, 64):
        corpus.append(_rand_token(r, L, L).encode())
    for L in (80, 120, 128):
        corpus.append(_rand_token(r, L, L).encode())
    for L in (200, 240, 256):
        corpus.append(_rand_token(r, L, L).encode())

    # 3) Path-like prefixes for append_query cases
    for _ in range(4):
        corpus.append(_rand_path_prefix(r).encode())

    # 4) Memcache-friendly keys (alnum plus separators) with mixed lengths
    for _ in range(6):
        corpus.append(_rand_token(r, 3, 40).encode())

    # 5) Empty string occasionally (some stubs fall back to defaults if empty)
    corpus.append(b"")

    # 6) Couple of numeric-like strings for exptime/delta as strings when misused
    for v in (b"0", b"1", b"60", b"300", b"86400", b"999999"):
        corpus.append(v)

    # 7) Mixed-case HTTP-ish tokens that could be used as query keys
    for t in ("User", "SessionID", "AuthToken", "sort", "filter", "lang", "q1", "q2"):
        corpus.append(t.encode())

    # Deduplicate while preserving order and limit total size later when packing
    seen = set()
    uniq: List[bytes] = []
    for it in corpus:
        if it not in seen:
            uniq.append(it)
            seen.add(it)
    return uniq


def _pack_chunks_with_lengths(chunks: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Simple length-prefixed concatenation: [count][len][data]...
    # Many fuzz harnesses read FUZZ_PARAM_STR from a data provider that splits arbitrarily,
    # but providing length-prefixed chunks allows custom providers to fetch deterministic slices.
    # Format:
    #  - 2 bytes: number of chunks (unsigned little-endian)
    #  - For each chunk: 2 bytes length (little-endian), then data bytes
    # Keep under 4096 bytes total.
    out = bytearray()
    # Reserve space for count
    out.extend(b"\x00\x00")
    count = 0
    for ch in chunks:
        if len(ch) > 65535:
            ch = ch[:65535]
        entry = len(ch).to_bytes(2, "little") + ch
        if len(out) + len(entry) > 4096:
            break
        out.extend(entry)
        count += 1
    out[0:2] = count.to_bytes(2, "little")
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    chunks = _build_corpus(r)

    # Shuffle to vary which tokens are consumed first, but keep some common tokens at front.
    # Keep first few stable seeds, shuffle the rest.
    head = chunks[:8]
    tail = chunks[8:]
    r.shuffle(tail)

    # Optionally insert a few composed k=v pieces that, if used as FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME or STR,
    # will still be safe identifiers after sanitization in the stub.
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        k = _rand_token(r, 1, 12)
        v = _rand_token(r, 0, 24, allow_empty=True)
        comp = f"{k}={v}".encode()
        tail.insert(r.randrange(len(tail)+1), comp)

    packed = _pack_chunks_with_lengths(head + tail)
    return packed
